51047812.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to ERK2 (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry
51047812.references_previous: Reference 9: Ruben, A. J.; Kiso, Y.; Freire, E. Overcoming roadblocks in lead optimization: a thermodynamic perspective. Chem. Biol. Drug Des. 2006, 67, 2–4.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC: ITC. Detailed calorimetric analysis was conducted in a iTC200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. KSI at 450 μM was titrated with fragments (5–10 mM) in PBS buffer supplemented with 5% DMSO. Data analysis was performed with the program ORIGIN7. Enthalpic efficiency EE was calculated as described earlier: EE = ΔH°/N where ΔH° is the standard enthalpy and N is the number of non-hydrogen atoms in the fragment molecule.

51047814.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Pseudomonas putida KSI by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Experimental Section - ITC: Detailed calorimetric analysis was conducted in a iTC200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. KSI at 450 μM was titrated with fragments (5–10 mM) in PBS buffer supplemented with 5% DMSO. Data analysis was performed with the program ORIGIN7. Enthalpic efficiency EE was calculated as described earlier: EE = ΔH°/N where ΔH° is the standard enthalpy and N is the number of non-hydrogen atoms in the fragment molecule.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Figure 2. Binding of DOC (positive control) to KSI. (a) Comparison of the structure of KSI in the apo form (orange) and with DOC bound (blue and green). (b) Real-time sensorgrams of the binding of DOC (analyte) to a CMS sensor chip decorated with KSI at the concentrations indicated. (c) K_D was calculated by the Scatchard method using the SPR responses in equilibrium. (d) Thermodynamic characterization by ITC. KSI (500 μM) was titrated with DOC (5 mM). Top and lower panels correspond to the titration kinetics and the binding isotherm, respectively. Regression analysis with the program ORIGIN7 is indicated with a red trace (bottom panel).
original_paragraph.Results Section - ITC data for DOC: ITC data indicate that the binding of DOC is driven by favorable enthalpy (ΔH = −2.2 ± 0.1 kcal mol−1) and entropy (−TΔS = −4.3 kcal mol−1) (Supporting Information Table S2).
